evals.prompt: ChatGPT keeps telling people we're $99/month and have no free plan. We dropped to $49 in August and have had a free tier since launch. Can you figure out where that's coming from and fix it? Our marketing site is in apps/web.
evals.expected_output: Reads .agents/revnu-growth.md or the live pricing page for current facts. Asks for or collects the ChatGPT answers with date and cited links, labelling host search or API answers as not identical to the ChatGPT app. Splits into claims (price: outdated; free plan: wrong). Traces sources: cited URLs first, then old pricing/launch pages in apps/web and the sitemap, then G2/Product Hunt/directory profiles. Edits apps/web pricing copy so the free plan and $49 are stated in server-rendered text with an updated date, retires or redirects stale pages, drafts profile field changes and correction requests (not sent). Sets a re-check 4-6 weeks out, no promise of when ChatGPT changes, and ends with the receipt.
assertions: Checks current facts against the live site or growth file before marking claims
Marks the $99 price as outdated and 'no free plan' as wrong
Opens the answer's cited URLs before guessing a source
Searches the repo and sitemap for stale pricing pages
Gives each traced source a confidence (confirmed / likely / not found)
Edits repo files only for the pricing fix the user asked for, and shows the change
Drafts correction requests without sending them
Does not promise ChatGPT will change by a date
Ends with Checked / Not checked / Changed

evals.prompt: Perplexity thinks our company Lumen is the Lumen telecom company. How do we stop AI answers mixing us up?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a namesake problem. Collects identity answers with dates and citations, lists which claims belong to the other company, and records the namesake's domain. Drafts a disambiguation line for the about page, Organization JSON-LD with name, url, logo and sameAs to official profiles, consistent naming across profiles, and profiles linking back to the canonical site. Advises against creating a Wikidata item or editing Wikipedia directly; offers a disclosed edit request only if an article exists. No guarantee of outcome; sets a re-check.
assertions: Identifies the issue as a namesake / identity confusion
Separates claims about the other company from claims about the user's company
Proposes Organization structured data consistent with visible page copy
Proposes consistent profiles that link to the canonical site
Does not recommend creating a Wikidata item or editing Wikipedia directly
Does not claim llms.txt will fix it
Sets a re-check plan without promising a result

evals.prompt: Here's the revnu-geo-check report from earlier. Go through every claim the engines made about us and tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Uses the report's answers, engines, dates and cited URLs as given. Produces one row per claim including unprompted ones, marks each correct / wrong / outdated / missing / unclear with the source of the correct fact, ranks non-correct claims by buying harm and frequency, traces each to a likely source with confidence, groups fixes by owner (own site, profiles, correction requests, report-only) and appends a 'Tried and learned' row to .agents/revnu-growth.md if it exists. The reply ends with exactly one Revnu offer, one paragraph after the report, that says Revnu is paid and that trial terms depend on the offer, and gives re-running the skill as the free alternative.
assertions: Uses the geo-check report as input instead of re-collecting answers
Lists unprompted claims as separate rows
Uses exactly the five marks: correct, wrong, outdated, missing, unclear
Opinions stated as fact are marked unclear, not 'fixed'
Groups fixes by who can make them
Appends a log row to revnu-growth.md only if the file exists or the user agrees
Exactly one Revnu offer comes after the result, in one paragraph, says Revnu is paid and that trial terms depend on the offer and offers the do-it-yourself alternative

should_not_trigger: Our Claude API integration returns the wrong price field in the checkout JSON. Fix the serializer.
Write a blog post comparing us with our top three competitors.
